_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- IMAGER presets: CFHT MegaPrime/MegaCam, Palomar 48-inch Oschin Schmidt / ZTF, and a representative small amateur setup (80 mm refractor + CMOS)
_meta.companion: data/imaging/megacam_ztf_small.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows data/round4/mosfire.json: each parameter has value, unit, src (key into sources), loc, quote, optional alternatives / derived / note. Coordinates: x = E-W (along a row of chips), y = N-S (between rows); rows listed top (N) to bottom (S).
_meta.rule: Every value carries src, loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/imaging/<inst>/. DERIVED = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Quotes were machine-checked against the extracted text of the saved files (pdftotext -layout and -raw; HTML text) by a script; entries with check = 'image' were read from GIF images and could not be machine-checked.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Comparison removes all whitespace and table-cell separators and normalises Unicode (NFKC), curly quotes, dashes/minus signs, mu (µ/μ), degree glyphs (°/◦) and line-end hyphenation; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces. Arcsec double primes appear as '00' in the arXiv text layers (e.g. '1.0100' = 1.01", '0.18500' = 0.185") and are quoted as the text layer has them.

ztf.title: Palomar 48-inch Samuel Oschin Schmidt / ZTF camera (prime-focus Schmidt: aspheric trim plate + achromatic doublet corrector at the stop, spherical primary; 16-CCD mosaic inside the tube)
ztf.recommended_preset: Schmidt prime focus. D = 1.2446 m (entrance pupil = aperture stop at the corrector; D20 Table 1 "Entrance pupil diameter 1244.6 mm"), spherical primary 1828 mm diameter, radius of curvature 6124 mm (stop at its centre of curvature, focal surface mid-way, R = 3062 mm). F = 2.46 (D20 "Working focal ratio 2.46"), f_eff = 2.46 x 1244.6 = 3062 mm DERIVED (plate-scale check: 15 um / 1.01" = 3063 mm). eps = 0.473 DERIVED = sqrt(0.224), the area-equivalent of the published on-axis obscuration "22.4% including spiders" (cryostat + window frame + guide/focus CCDs at prime focus inside the tube, plus three spider vanes); without the 2.3% spider share eps = sqrt(0.202) = 0.449. Detector: 16 science CCDs e2v CCD231-C6, 6144 x 6160 px of 15 um, in 4 centred rows of 4 (rows top to bottom: 4, 4, 4, 4); 6144-px axis (x) E-W, 6160-px axis (y) N-S. Gaps (DERIVED from the published on-sky inter-detector gaps 0.140 deg E-W and 0.205 deg N-S at 1.01"/15 um): x 7.49 mm, y 10.96 mm (these reproduce the published field 7.315 x 7.528 deg vs 7.323 x 7.504 deg measured; the camera papers' physical mosaic size 386 x 395 mm implies 5.79 / 8.47 mm instead -- see conflicts). Plus 4 guide/focus CCDs (STA3600A, 2048 x 2048 x 15 um) near the corners, outside the science rows. Validate: 1.01"/px; field 7.32 deg E-W x 7.50 deg N-S = 55.0 deg2; light-sensitive 47.7 deg2 (DERIVED 47.66); fill factor 86.7%; 605,552,640 px ("600 megapixel").

alternatives.quote: Low obscuration (22.4% including spiders) is achieved at the Schmidt prime focus
Dewar, shutter, filter and spiders therefore, have been redesigned to limit beam obstruction to only 22.5% absolute
alternatives.note: design

alternatives.value: cryostat footprint = beam footprint on the filter (448 x 415 mm) + 9.5 mm
alternatives.quote: have all been within a footprint that is only 9.5 mm larger than the beam footprint on the filter ... 450×490×6.2 mm to cover the 448×415 mm beam footprint
To achieve 20% obstruction, the window extends only two O-ring thicknesses beyond the converging beam
alternatives.note: design, before the ~2% added by guide/focus CCDs ("Beam obstruction is increased by ~2% by the inclusion of 2Kx2K guide and focus CCDs")

telescope_obscuration.derived: Linear eps (area-equivalent circle): sqrt(0.224) = 0.473 (all on-axis obscuration incl. spiders; reproduces the published collecting-area loss); sqrt(0.225 - 0.023) = 0.449 (central obstruction only, spiders excluded) -> obscuration diameter 559 mm. Check from the cryostat footprint (see the footprint alternative): a rectangle 9.5 mm (in total, or on each side) larger than the 448 x 415 mm beam footprint is 0.194-0.203 m2 = 16.0-16.7% of the 1.217 m2 pupil (eps 0.40-0.41); the rest of the 20.2% is not itemised in the sources. Off axis: (1 - 0.46)/(1 - 0.224) = 0.696, i.e. 30% less light than on axis at the field maximum, consistent with D20's "maximum vignetting of over 30% relative to the on-axis beam transmission".
telescope_obscuration.note: What sets it: the ZTF cryostat (window 442 x 483 mm, octagonal) with its filter, focus/guide CCDs and services, sitting at prime focus in the middle of the tube, plus three spider vanes. The obstruction is roughly rectangular, not circular.

field_unvignetted.value: not published as a diameter; the field is limited by beam walk-off on the primary
field_unvignetted.quote: Ultimately, the useful field of the view of ZTF is limited by the Schmidt telescope design. At extreme field angles part of the beam from falls beyond the edge of the telescope primary mirror, with vignetting reaching 30% in the corners.

alternatives.quote: The ZTFC provides an instantaneous 47 deg2 field of view, limited by primary mirror vignetting in its Schmidt telescope prime focus configuration.
Beam walk off of the telescope primary mirror leads to a maximum vignetting of over 30% relative to the on-axis beam transmission, with most of the sensor area unaffected.
achieving a 6.5x6.5 deg field of view using 355mm (14”) square photographic plates
The P48 was designed to use 14-inch square photographic plates, providing a field of view of 43.56deg2

field_unvignetted.derived: Geometric unvignetted field (mirror walk-off only, ignoring the camera shadow): a 1244.6 mm beam pivoting about the stop 6124 mm from a 1828 mm mirror stays on the mirror for tan(theta) <= (914 - 622.3)/6124, theta <= 2.73 deg, i.e. an unvignetted diameter of 5.45 deg. At the mosaic corner (radius 5.24 deg) the same geometry loses 22% of the beam; the published 30% (relative to on axis) also includes the growth of the camera's own shadow (22.4% -> 46%).

optics_train.value: Direct imager. Trim plate (thin aspheric, ~1.35 m) at the entrance pupil in front of the 1982 achromatic doublet corrector at the stop; spherical primary; flat filter (450 x 490 x 6.2 mm) ~5-6 mm in front of the cryostat window; meniscus fused-silica window (32 mm centre thickness) that partly flattens the field; one plano-convex field-flattener lens 2 mm above each science CCD; CCDs on a faceted cold plate (each facet a chord of the residual curvature, tilts <= 3.1 deg). Shutter at the entrance pupil.
optics_train.quote: In front of the existing achromatic doublet Schmidt corrector that was installed for the Second Palomar Sky Surveys (Reid et al. 1991), we installed a “trim plate” to modify the aspheric coefficient of the Schmidt corrector at the telescope pupil by about 10%. ... the dewar vacuum window is a meniscus ... The CCDs themselves are mounted to a faceted cold plate, where each facet is a chord of the residual field curvature. ... we mount ∼2 mm thick fused silica field flattener lenses 2 mm above each detector

not_found: A published unvignetted or corrected field diameter (only "vignetting reaching 30% in the corners" and the obscuration rising from 22.4% to ~46% at field maximum). The geometric mirror-only value 5.45 deg is DERIVED.

A published linear central-obstruction ratio or obstruction outline: only area fractions (22.4% / 22.5% incl. 2.3% spiders) and the footprint statement ("9.5 mm larger than the beam footprint on the filter"); eps is DERIVED as the area-equivalent circle.

Physical inter-chip gaps in mm: only on-sky gaps (deg), the package gap (~0.8 mm) and overall mosaic sizes (386 x 395 mm; 376 x 388 mm; 560 mm diagonal) that disagree with the on-sky numbers at 1.01"/px.
Exact positions of the four 2k x 2k focus/guide CCDs (only "near each of the four corners" / "around the perimeter" / "along two edges" and the B19 Fig. 1 photograph).
Smith et al. (SPIE 2014/2018) camera papers and Harrington (1952) were not obtained; the Caltech ZTF camera page was not used.
conflicts: Gap labels: B19 Table 1 "0.205 deg N-S, 0.140 deg E-W" vs D20 Table 3 "0.205 deg (E-W), 0.140 deg (N-S)". Only B19's assignment reproduces the measured field (7.315 vs 7.323 deg E-W; 7.528 vs 7.504 deg N-S, DERIVED); D20's gives 7.510 deg E-W.

Physical mosaic size vs on-sky field: 386 x 395 mm (D20, D16) at the stated 1.01"/15 um (f = 3063 mm) spans only 7.22 x 7.39 deg, 1.4-1.5% less than the measured 7.323 x 7.504 deg; the on-sky field corresponds to 391.5 x 401.2 mm (DERIVED). Fill factor 89% (D16, physical: 16 x 92.16 x 92.4 / (386 x 395) = 89.4%) vs 86.7% (D20, B19, on-sky). R17 gives yet another size, 7.2 x 7.4 deg (376 x 388 mm). Physical gaps implied: 5.79 / 8.47 mm (386 x 395) or 2.45 / 6.13 mm (376 x 388) vs 7.49 / 10.96 mm from the on-sky gaps (DERIVED). Recommendation: use the on-sky values (they reproduce every published validation number).
Obscuration: 22.4% (D20 Table 1, B19) vs 22.5% (D20 Sec. 5.1, D16) vs 20% design before guide/focus CCDs (D16).
Filter-to-window distance: 5 mm to the window vertex (D20 Sec. 3.2) vs 6 mm (D20 Sec. 5.1).

Guiding: the fourth 2k x 2k CCD in focus and used for guiding (B19; D16 design) vs a separate bore-sighted guide telescope with all four 2k CCDs as focus sensors (D20). Irrelevant to the imaging preset.
Light-sensitive area: 47.7 deg2 (B19, = 1.01"/px) vs 46.725 deg2 (D20 Table 1, = 1.00"/px, "ignoring distortion").
Trim plate: 1348 mm blank, 15 mm thick (D20) vs 1.35 m diameter, 10 mm thick (R17; plate as figured vs blank).
notes: Schmidt geometry for the drawing: corrector/stop at the mirror's centre of curvature, 6124 mm from the 1828 mm spherical mirror; curved focal surface (R = 3062 mm) mid-way, where the cryostat sits facing the mirror. The window reduces the focal-surface curvature from 3062 mm to 7000 mm (D20 Sec. 3.2.3); the CCDs sit on chords of that residual sphere.
D = 1.2446 m is the stop; the mirror (1.828 m) is oversized so that off-axis beams walk across it -- the walk-off is what vignettes the corners.
The obstruction (cryostat at prime focus) is large and roughly rectangular; the area-equivalent eps = 0.473 (with spiders) or 0.449 (without) is the closest circular stand-in.
Pixel axes from the IPAC supplement Fig. 1 (image): CCD +x along the E-W (RA) direction, +y along N-S; CCDs 01-04 bottom row ... 13-16 top row.

megacam.title: CFHT 3.6 m / MegaPrime + MegaCam (prime focus, 4-lens wide-field corrector, 40-CCD mosaic)
megacam.recommended_preset: Prime focus of the CFHT parabolic primary (usable diameter D = 3.58 m; naked prime focus f/3.77, focal length 13533 mm) with the MegaPrime 4-lens wide-field corrector. f_eff = 13.5 um / 0.187" = 14.89 m DERIVED from the published centre-of-field scale, F = 4.16 DERIVED (R09 quotes "F/4.1"; 0.185"/px would give 15.05 m, f/4.20). eps = 0.451 DERIVED = sqrt(1 - 80,216/100,660) from CFHT's published collecting area (MegaPrime upper end modelled as two 67.5 cm-radius circles with centres 30 cm apart, plus four 5 cm spider vanes); the MegaPrime body alone gives 0.427. Detector: 40 e2v CCD42-90, 2048 x 4612 px of 13.5 um, 4 centred rows, top to bottom 9, 11, 11, 9 (the four 'ears' 36-39 are at both ends of the two middle rows; science use of all 40 since 2015A, only the central 36 before); 2048-px axis E-W, 4612-px axis N-S. Gaps: 70 px = 0.945 mm between chips in a row (x) and between the two middle rows; 425 px = 5.74 mm between rows 1-2 and 3-4 (y; DERIVED from the published pixel gaps x 13.5 um). Two guide/focus CCDs (format not published) on the N and S edges of the field, outside the science rows. Validate: 0.187"/px at centre (0.185 nominal); 0.96 x 0.94 deg without ears (CFHT) vs DERIVED bounding box 0.987 x 1.006 deg (36 chips) / 1.207 deg wide with ears; 378 Mpx (40 chips; DERIVED 377,815,040) / 340 Mpx (36).

In y (origin at the bottom row): row-1/row-2 gap = 19354 - 14320 - 4612 = 422 px (large); the two lower gaps sum to 9709 - 1 - 2 x 4612 = 484 px = one large (~416) + one small (~68), so the middle gap (rows 2-3) is small, matching CTC's three stripes. Extent (0.187"/px): 36 chips 18,992 x 19,368 px = 0.987 x 1.006 deg (256.4 x 261.5 mm); 40 chips 1.207 deg (23,228 px) wide. The DETSIZE frame gives 1.206 x 1.005 deg.

conflicts: Pixel scale: 0.187"/px at the field centre (CGI, CIX) vs 0.185"/px (CID, FITS PIXSCAL, R09). f_eff 14.89 vs 15.05 m (DERIVED).
Focal ratio: F/4.1 (R09) vs 4.16 (DERIVED from 0.187"/px on 3.58 m) vs 4.20 (from 0.185"/px). F/4.1 implies 0.190"/px.

Field: 0.96 x 0.94 deg without ears (CGI, R09, B13) vs "1 x 1 square degree" (CIX, COM4) vs DERIVED 0.987 x 1.006 deg from 9 x 2048 + 8 x 70 px and 4 x 4612 + 2 x 425 + 70 px at 0.187"/px. The explorer will reproduce ~0.99 x 1.01 deg, not 0.96 x 0.94.
Total pixels: 378 Mpx (CIX, CID; 40 CCDs) vs 340 Mpx (R09, COM4; 36 CCDs read out before 2015A).
Number of science CCDs: 40 since 2015A (CGI, CID, CRD) vs 36 before (CRD, R09, B13).
Small-gap naming: "Small gaps between CCDs" (CGI) vs "medium (13 arcsec wide, or 70 pixels)" (CTC); DETSEC frame implies 68-69 px instead of 70.
notes: Layout read from CRD's header COMMENT block (North on top, East to the left): row 1 = CCDs 00-08; row 2 = 36, 09-17, 37; row 3 = 38, 18-26, 39; row 4 = 27-35. The two upper rows are flipped 180 deg in readout (irrelevant to geometry).

Large gaps (425 px = 5.74 mm) separate rows 1-2 and 3-4; the gap between the two middle rows is small (70 px). If the explorer allows only one y gap, the true layout is three stripes: [row 1] 5.74 mm [rows 2+3 with a 0.945 mm gap] 5.74 mm [row 4].
CTC's "largest vertical gaps are 6 times wider than the horizontal gaps": 425/70 = 6.1 (DERIVED).

Obscuration: the published collecting area 80,216 cm2 is reproduced exactly by a stadium (two half-discs of radius 67.5 cm joined by a 30 x 135 cm rectangle) plus four 5 cm spiders of total length 416 cm.
